questions.q: Where should a company avoid cutting costs?
a: In the capabilities that genuinely set it apart from rivals
In the departments that spend the most each year
In the areas with the newest and least proven staff
In every part of the business until profits recover
questions.why: Lesson 1 says cuts should protect what makes the company better than others.

questions.q: Why does the book say to start reducing expenses today?
a: A crisis may force hasty cuts that damage your strengths
Investors reward companies that announce cuts early
Costs always rise faster than revenue over time
Employees work harder when budgets are shrinking
questions.why: Lesson 2 says unprepared firms slash their differentiating capabilities in a panic.

questions.q: What does a company's footprint mean here?
a: Every location where the organization runs any activity
The total carbon emissions produced by its factories
The number of customers it serves in each country
The share of the market it controls locally
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines it as all sites, from service centers to research labs.

questions.q: What must a low-wage country offer before a company relocates work there?
a: Enough skilled people and reliable infrastructure
The lowest possible wage levels anywhere in the region
A large domestic market for the company's products
Tax breaks that last for at least ten years
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that weak talent or infrastructure can cost more than it saves.

questions.q: What happens to companies that try to be best at everything?
a: They spread resources thin and end up mediocre at everything
They grow faster because no department is neglected
They attract stronger leaders in every function
They reduce risk by avoiding dependence on one skill
questions.why: Lesson 1 says equal spending across departments leaves no real advantage.
